title: Companion renderer modes, capability loss and capability restoration, on a real GPU
notRunReason: No physical machine with a real GPU is available. Every renderer measurement this project holds was taken under llvmpipe.
prerequisite: H1 must have reached H1.7. A renderer result on a live-booted system is not a result about an installed one.

steps.expect: the 3D renderer starts on the real GPU and interaction works
steps.failIf: the GL renderer string names llvmpipe or softpipe -- that is not a real-GPU result and must be recorded as such rather than as a 3D pass

steps.step: capability loss: rendering capability becomes unavailable while 3D is the preference
steps.expect: a safe fallback activates AND the stored 3D preference is NOT destroyed
steps.failIf: the preference is rewritten to the fallback mode. Silently destroying the preference is the defect this step exists to catch, and a system that falls back cleanly while forgetting what the user chose FAILS.

steps.expect: the preferred mode can recover, either automatically or by an action the user can find
steps.failIf: recovery requires editing a file, or the preference has to be re-set by hand

steps.expect: renders and animates correctly on the real panel
steps.failIf: frames are identical across an animation, or the character's working pose is wrong -- coverage assertions have passed on a shrug before

steps.expect: switching between all three modes works in both directions without a restart
steps.failIf: any transition requires a restart, or leaves the previous renderer's resources allocated

required: startup time to first frame, per mode
idle CPU with the Companion HIDDEN
idle CPU with the Companion VISIBLE
conditions: Each measurement records the GL vendor and renderer string alongside it. A number without that string cannot be compared with anything.

Hidden and visible idle are measured separately and never averaged. The whole open performance question is whether redraw cost explains the regression, and averaging the two destroys the only signal that could answer it.
The VM comparator is recorded next to each figure and labelled llvmpipe, so no reader mistakes one for the other.

gradingRules: A measurement taken under llvmpipe may NEVER be presented as a real-GPU result. If H2.1 finds llvmpipe, every measurement in this journey is a VM measurement and the journey is NOT_RUN for its stated purpose.
H2.2 fails on preference destruction even if the fallback itself is flawless.
Every step must resolve. A mode not exercised is NOT_RUN.
